note: 'Fanny' was educated at home; 'she married a young attorney, Blewett Lee, at 19. The couple had three children and at first appeared happy, but Glessner Lee eventually received a divorce. Their son attributed the failed marriage partly to her creative urge coupled with high manual dexterity—the desire to make things—which [Lee] did not share.' In 1931 she endowed a department of legal medicine at Harvard; she built the Nutshell Studies of Unexplained Death in the 1930s and '40s at one inch to a foot, and suggested a clockwise spiral to search a scene; she wrote to an adviser, 'I found myself constantly tempted to add more clues and details…stop me when I go too far.' The quotation of the son is the article's.
